business_scope.primary_industry_name: Blank-Check Entity for Public Market Acquisition Mergers (SPAC)

Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the French Republic on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (2007)
Energy Charter Treaty (1994, France is a signatory)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L561-1 et seq. and R561-1 et seq.; Ordinance No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020; Decree No. 2020-118 of 12 February 2020; Code de commerce, Articles R123-235 through R123-242 (UBO declaration); Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on fund transfers; Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5) as transposed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Association (Statuts de la SARL)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French Notary (Notaire) in the place of the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) if executed in France and presented abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified True Copy of Passport (Shareholder, Manager, or Signatory)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of the country of origin (e.g., passport office, consulate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (non-Hague countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of Residential Address (Utility Bill or Bank Statement)
Certificate of Good Standing (Corporate Extract) for Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for Formation Agent (Procuration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of residence of the grantor

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Source of Funds Declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Apostille, or authenticated by the issuing bank and consular legalization if required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, shareholders, beneficial owners, managers, and authorized signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions lists, and the French domestic sanctions list maintained by the Direction générale du Trésor. Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) database checks (World-Check/Refinitiv, LexisNexis Diligence) must be performed to determine risk rating; all matches require enhanced due diligence, source of wealth verification, and approval from senior management. The French UBO register is not publicly accessible; access is limited to the financial intelligence unit (Tracfin), ACPR, AMF, notaires, and other authorized obliged entities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script using the Roman alphabet. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated phonetically into Latin characters. The legal form indicator 'SARL' or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' must appear on all official documents, and may be included in the registered name. The name must be distinguishable from existing trademarks and other company names, not misleading, and consistent with public order and good morals. French law does not require that the name be composed of French words; foreign names are permitted if written in Latin script.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the chosen name is unavailable or appears on the registry's list of invalid denominations, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal (recours) with the President of the Tribunal de Commerce within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must be lodged against the Registrar (greffier) and must set out the grounds for overturning the rejection. Alternatively, the applicant may modify the name and submit a new registration request via the INPI Guichet Unique; if the objection originates from a prior trademark, the applicant can either secure a letter of consent from the prior holder or replace the contested token with a non-conflicting term.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible for a SARL on a temporary basis for up to two years when domiciled at the manager's residence, or on a permanent basis via an authorized domiciliation company (domiciliataire) registered with the Registrar in the town of the effective establishment. For a special purpose acquisition company holding escrowed acquisition funds, the local commercial substance requirements are intensified; a mere virtual mailbox without a local real administrative seat and operational records will be red-flagged by French AML authorities and may trigger a denial of corporate benefits or license revocation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection during the first twelve months of operation for a SARL in the SPAC sector; the likelihood increases to approximately 70% when a virtual office arrangement is used and the company cannot contemporaneously evidence local management, personnel, or records.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company incorporation registration fee paid to INPI (Guichet Unique/RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI – Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (on behalf of RCS)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the formation notice (avis de constitution) in a legal gazette
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Accredited legal notice newspaper (Journal d'annonces légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory ceiling per line (approximately 18 EUR per line)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the articles of association and ancillary corporate instruments
Apostille legalization of foreign records (six documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs – Bureau des Apostilles (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign documents into French
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark (per page or per word)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT PEP and sanctions screening and UBO analysis
Drafting of SPAC acquisition charter and ancillary investment agreements
Bank escrow account setup and wiring of seed capital
Power of attorney notarization and appointment of formation signatory
Regulatory classification consultation (ACPR/AMF confirmation of non-eligible activity or license requirement)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL formation and governance); Decree No. 2020-106 (electronic filings)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and M0 form (déclaration de création d'entreprise)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital required for SARL; however, for SPAC purposes, a minimum paid-up capital of €1,000,000 (or equivalent in USD) must be escrowed in a dedicated trust account (compte séquestre) to satisfy listing and investor protection requirements
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the company be and is hereby incorporated as a Société à Responsabilité Limitée under the laws of France. The registered office is fixed at [address], Paris, France. The initial share capital of €[amount] is subscribed and paid in full by the shareholders, with funds deposited into the company's escrow trust account. The following persons are appointed as managers (gérants): [Name], [Name]. The managers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute all filings with the RCS, and engage legal counsel for the purpose of completing the SPAC listing process. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (notaire) or online legal platform (e.g., legalstart.fr) with subsequent filing to the Greffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts in French, including corporate name, registered office, share capital, share classes, management structure, and SPAC-specific clauses (trust account, redemption rights, acquisition timeline). If capital exceeds €1,000,000 or real estate is contributed, notarization is mandatory. Otherwise, private signed statuts are acceptable. Ensure all shareholders sign and initial each page.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of shareholders and managers (passport or national ID)
Proof of registered office address (lease or utility bill)
Bank certificate of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe rejects the statuts for missing clauses, amend the document and resubmit within 15 days. For notarized statuts, the notary will correct and re-certify.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish a Legal Notice in a French Official Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) – authorized legal gazette (e.g., Les Echos, Le Figaro)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice of incorporation containing the company name, legal form (SARL), capital amount, registered office, and purpose (SPAC). The notice must appear before filing with the RCS. Obtain a certificate of publication (attestation de parution) from the gazette.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette rejects the notice due to non-compliance with legal format, correct the text and republish. The publication is valid for 6 months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Dossier with the Commercial Court Registry (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) – online via Infogreffe or in-person
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed M0 form, statuts, legal notice publication certificate, and proof of capital deposit to the registry. The registry will verify the dossier and issue a K-bis extract (official company registration certificate). For SPAC entities, the registry may require additional documentation on the trust account and AML compliance.
required_dossiers: Bank deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
Declaration of no criminal record (bulletin n°3) for managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query (demande de pièces complémentaires), respond within 30 days with the missing documents. If the dossier is rejected, correct and resubmit. The registry may impose a penalty for late response.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain K-Bis Extract and Register for Tax and Social Security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; French Tax Authority (DGFiP); URSSAF (social security)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the K-Bis extract, the company is legally formed. Automatically, the registry transmits data to the tax authority for a SIRET number and to URSSAF for employer registration. For SPAC, the company must also register for VAT (if applicable) and corporate income tax (IS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SIRET number is not received within 10 days, contact the DGFP directly. For URSSAF, any delay may be cured by filing a late registration request.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité des Marchés Financiers (AMF) – for SPAC listing and public offering; Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFP) for financial licensing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Agrément de société de financement (financial institution approval) or AMF visa for public offering (visa AMF)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique (MTE) – Environmental Protection Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – SPAC is a financial holding entity with no physical industrial operations; however, if the SPAC acquires a target with industrial activities, a full EIA may be required at the target level
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at formation stage; if the SPAC later acquires an industrial target, compliance with French environmental code (Code de l'environnement) thresholds for wastewater (e.g., COD < 125 mg/L), VOC emissions (below 2 t/year), and hazardous waste handling (RCRA-equivalent) will be mandatory

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (attestation de sécurité incendie) for any physical office space; structural load inspection (contrôle technique) if the registered office is in a commercial building; workplace health and safety clearance (certificat de conformité) from the labor inspectorate (Inspection du Travail) for any employees

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SARL entities obtain SIREN/SIRET automatically upon RCS registration; foreign-owned entities register via guichet-entreprises.gouv.fr to secure SIREN prior to tax identification
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections; fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) available for qualifying French parent-subsidiary groups

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory Factur-X e-invoicing for B2B transactions since 2024; real-time fiscal reporting via tax authority platforms; integrated customs clearance for exports

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT on goods exported outside the EU with proof of removal from French territory; intra-EU supplies subject to reverse-charge rules
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims attract penalties up to 80% of evaded VAT plus interest; retrospective clawback with surcharges and potential criminal liability

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) acting in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) under the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Recovery
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France adopts the euro, which enjoys full convertibility for both current account and capital account transactions. No foreign exchange licensing is required for non-resident companies engaging in capital movements, and no prior central bank authorization applies to profit remittances or repatriation of invested capital. Restrictions are limited to national security FDI screening in sensitive sectors and periodic reporting for balance-of-payments statistics. Profit remittance is generally tax-transparent under the parent-subsidiary directive, subject to beneficial ownership proof and anti-tax-avoidance verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender rule and no mandatory conversion of foreign currency earned by French residents. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts. All cross-border settlements, including export proceeds, must be reported to the Banque de France via the resident intermediary bank for balance-of-payments statistics. Non-EU foreign currency balances are subject to annual customs declarations and may be required for corporate tax audits; however, no timeline for repatriation is imposed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low — French licensed EMI/fintech providers (e.g., Qonto, Shine) generally do not accept blank-check acquisition vehicles or SPAC structures due to their inherent money-laundering risk profile. Escrow funds from public subscriptions must be placed in prudentially regulated credit institutions under the AMF (Autorité des Marchés Financiers) rules; EMIs lack the authority to hold such escrow deposits. Limited cross-border utility exists for low-volume operational expenses, but not for the core treasury and clearing functions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For EU-resident legal representatives and major shareholders, remote video-based identification is legally accepted in France if performed by a licensed identification service or a notary. For non-EU resident sponsors and US-based directors, most tier-1 French banks will require a physical interview either at the company’s registered office or at the bank’s branch. A fully remote opening without notarized copies or apostilled powers of attorney is usually not accepted for a SPAC due to the enhanced due diligence framework.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Blank-check/SPAC legal form with no operating business and future unknown target
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SPAC charter, prospectus approved by AMF, bank account purpose letter, detailed acquisition policy, target sector description, term commitment, and investor protection undertakings

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geographic concentrations of non-EU investors or indirectly held US shell entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership chain with individual beneficial owners (>25%), corporate registers extract, passport copies with notarization, source-of-wealth declaration, and supported bank references from upstream banks

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large overnight trust or escrow deposits without clear economic origin
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed subscription agreements, escrow agent appointment deed, proof of funds from audited accounts or securities statements, and contractual explanation of the SPAC’s capital buildup in the pre-IPO period

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons (PEPs) among directors or sponsors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP self-declaration forms, independent background checks, professional and tax reference letters, and compliance acceptance from the bank’s hierarchical compliance committee

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from foreign sponsors or IPO subscriptions must be routed via SWIFT MT103 with clear purpose codes classified as 'direct investments' or 'capital increase' under the Banque de France’s balance-of-payments nomenclature. Each wire must include the SPAC’s legal name, the purpose reference (e.g., 'Subscriptions in escrow'), and the individual investor’s identifier. The receiving French bank will require a copy of the escrow agreement and a certificate from a notary or accountant confirming the share issue. All movements above EUR 1,000 are automatically captured in the French balance-of-payments reporting system via the intermediary bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for the SPAC’s acquisition of a target company are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for cash payments directly to target shareholders’ accounts. If a commercial letter of credit is used, it would apply only to post-acquisition trade operations, not to the equity acquisition itself. For acquisition disbursements, the bank will require the notarial transfer deed, board resolutions, AMF statement if triggered, and tax clearance certificates (attestation de régularité fiscale) to release funds. Under French AML rules, all payment legs must quote the underlying transaction and identify the ultimate beneficiary.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-EUR emerging market currency exposure
Currency options (plain vanilla, cost-effective for hedging acquisition price uncertainty)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Bilan and Compte de Résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15th day of the 4th month following the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of 0.5% of annual turnover per month of delay (maximum 5%), administrative fines up to €10,000, and potential company dissolution proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SARL exceeds two of the following criteria: turnover exceeding €50 million, balance sheet total exceeding €43 million, or average headcount exceeding 50 employees
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (PCG) unless IFRS is elected under specific conditions

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Notification of any changes in Ultimate Beneficial Owners or shareholdings to the greffe within one month; no statutory annual confirmation required but annual review of UBO status is standard practice

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 100 to 400 USD annually for registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 to 3,000 USD for non-audit required SARLs; higher if statutory audit mandated

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). A reduced 15% rate may apply to qualifying small and medium-sized companies on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory shareholding, turnover and capital conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying SMEs may apply the 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit. France generally provides no broad corporate tax holiday for a standard SARL or SPAC acquisition vehicle. Eligible research and development expenditure may qualify for the research tax credit, generally at 30% of eligible expenditure incurred in metropolitan France up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to detailed eligibility and documentation. Certain innovation, investment, regional and restructuring incentives may apply only if statutory conditions are satisfied.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward, subject to an annual utilization cap generally equal to EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Carryback is generally limited to the immediately preceding financial year and capped at the lower of the preceding year's profit and EUR 1 million. Significant changes in business activity, mergers, or tax-neutral reorganizations may restrict or terminate the use of losses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, with tax package forms 2058-A-SD through 2059-G-SD and, where relevant, 2066-SD, 2067-SD, 2079-CICE-SD or other applicable schedules. Electronic filing is generally mandatory through the DGFiP professional portal espace professionnel or through an authorized EDI-TDFC provider. A separate annual balance-of-tax-payment form, Form 2572-SD, is generally used for the final corporate income tax settlement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; quarterly corporate income tax installments are payment obligations rather than separate income tax returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the annual return is generally due by the second business day following 1 May of the following year, subject to the officially published filing calendar and any standard electronic filing tolerance. For a financial year ending on another date, filing is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. The final corporate income tax balance is generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end, or by 15 May for a 31 December year-end, subject to applicable electronic-payment rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the legal name, registered office, SIREN number, principal activity, financial year start and end dates, tax office, and legal form as Société à Responsabilité Limitée.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or parent is not substituted for the French SARL. Report the French legal entity and its French tax identification details. Identify any French permanent establishment or French fixed place of business separately where relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, taxable result and corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable profit or tax loss determined from French statutory accounts after tax adjustments, the applicable 25% rate, any eligible 15% SME-rate profit, tax credits, instalments and balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income and expenses attributable to the French taxpayer under French tax rules. Deductibility of payments to non-residents requires business purpose, arm's-length support, withholding analysis and evidence of actual services or financing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit or loss to taxable profit through permanent and temporary additions and deductions, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation differences, exempt income and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for French limitations on interest deductions, hybrid instruments, non-deductible distributions, controlled transactions and expenses lacking sufficient substantiation. Apply treaty exemptions only after confirming the relevant legal conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax losses carried forward, losses utilized in the current year, losses carried back where elected, and remaining losses subject to the annual utilization limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign group losses generally cannot be used directly by the French SARL. Preserve continuity of business and ownership documentation where losses are expected to survive a restructuring or acquisition.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2058-C-SD, exempt or specially taxed income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report items excluded from ordinary taxable profit or subject to special regimes, including qualifying participation exemption adjustments and certain tax-neutral restructuring items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends, capital gains and payments involving foreign affiliates must be tested under the French participation exemption, parent-subsidiary regime, treaty and anti-abuse rules before any exclusion is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Forms 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, capital gains and depreciable assets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report disposals, capital gains, depreciation, provisions and relevant asset movements, including assets acquired or disposed of in an acquisition or listing structure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document acquisition basis, fair value, related-party transfers, financing costs and the allocation of transaction expenses. Asset transfers involving foreign affiliates require arm's-length valuation support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim foreign tax credits only where permitted by French domestic law or an applicable tax treaty, with the relevant foreign income and tax evidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident owner cannot claim the French SARL's foreign tax credits personally through the SARL return. Credits must be claimed by the legally entitled taxpayer and supported by withholding certificates or equivalent official evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile tax installments, tax credits, withholding credits and the final corporate income tax balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the French entity's bank mandate and electronic payment account are active. Non-resident shareholders generally cannot pay or file on behalf of the company without properly documented authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report and retain information on controlled transactions, related-party financing, services, royalties, guarantees, cash pooling, acquisitions and disposals. Additional transfer pricing returns or declarations may apply where statutory thresholds are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain intercompany agreements, functional analyses, invoices, beneficial ownership information, pricing calculations and evidence of services received. French tax authorities may disregard undocumented charges or recharacterize them as distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile corporate income tax revenue and expenses with VAT returns, payroll filings, customs records and statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident SPAC sponsor must not assume that an absence of French VATable operations eliminates French filing duties. Fixed establishment, management services, acquisition services and transaction fees require separate VAT analysis.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may trigger an automatic 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% where the return is not filed within 30 days after a formal notice, and potentially 80% in cases involving fraudulent or abusive conduct. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge plus late-payment interest, commonly calculated at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory changes and procedural relief. Inaccurate returns may result in tax reassessment, interest, surcharges of 40% for deliberate omission, 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of law, and criminal prosecution in serious tax-fraud cases.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2777-SD for withholding taxes on certain movable-income distributions and related payments, filed electronically through the DGFiP professional portal or EDI channel where required. Dividend withholding and other payment-specific declarations may require additional schedules depending on the recipient, payment type and applicable exemption.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Payment-event or monthly filing, generally due by the 15th day of the month following the month of payment, subject to the specific income category and current administrative instructions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Withholding tax is generally remitted when the payment is made or made available, with the related declaration and payment due within the statutory period applicable to Form 2777-SD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the French SARL's SIREN, legal name, address, tax office and payment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SARL remains the withholding agent even where the recipient is a non-resident parent, sponsor, lender or service provider.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2777-SD, payment category and gross amount
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classify the payment as dividend, interest, royalty or another reportable income category and enter the gross amount before withholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not net expenses, bank fees or foreign taxes from the gross amount unless French law specifically permits the adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2777-SD, domestic rate, treaty rate or exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the domestic withholding rate or the reduced treaty or directive rate, together with the legal basis and supporting documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply a reduced rate only after obtaining the required residence certificate, beneficial-owner evidence, eligibility declarations and, where applicable, advance approval or French tax-authority documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold or remit may create primary tax liability against the French payer, late-payment interest, a 10% late or omitted filing surcharge and higher surcharges for deliberate or fraudulent conduct. The payer may also be liable for compensation of the recipient's tax cost if the contract contains a gross-up obligation.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident, subject to domestic exemptions, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in France, and an applicable tax treaty. A qualifying EU or EEA corporate parent may generally obtain a 0% rate if minimum ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. Treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 15%, but the applicable bilateral treaty controls.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a current certificate of tax residence from the recipient's competent tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, legal form, minimum ownership and holding-period conditions, and collect any prescribed declaration or certificate required for the relevant treaty or EU exemption. The French payer must retain evidence and apply the correct rate on the payment date. Where relief at source is unavailable or uncertain, withhold at the domestic rate and pursue refund through the applicable French claim procedure. Anti-conduit, principal-purpose, beneficial-owner and general anti-abuse rules must be considered. A treaty residence certificate does not by itself establish treaty entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties and similar payments to non-residents are generally subject to a 25% withholding tax under domestic rules, subject to treaty reduction or exemption and possible 75% treatment for payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but exceptions may apply, including payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, anti-abuse situations and specific income categories. Treaty interest rates commonly range from 0% to 15%; treaty royalty rates commonly range from 0% to 10% or 15%. The applicable treaty, beneficial ownership, residence certificate and anti-abuse conditions must be reviewed for each payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million. A French entity generally falls within the full transfer pricing documentation regime where its annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets reach EUR 400 million, where it belongs to a group meeting the threshold, or where specified controlled-transaction conditions apply. A Local File and Master File based on OECD concepts are required for qualifying taxpayers. A simplified transfer pricing declaration and supporting documentation may apply below the full threshold. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to the French reporting entity of an international group meeting the EUR 750 million consolidated revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations applicable to every holding or financing company. Substance is nevertheless tested through transfer pricing, beneficial ownership, anti-abuse and principal-purpose rules, controlled foreign company provisions, interest limitation, hybrid mismatch rules, management-and-control principles and the French abuse-of-law doctrine. A French SARL acting as a SPAC acquisition vehicle should maintain genuine French governance, documented board decision-making, appropriate personnel or outsourced functions under effective French supervision, French accounting and banking records, commercial rationale, risk control and evidence that financing, acquisition and advisory activities actually occur as reported.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing taxable income, fabricating expenses, submitting false accounts, understating distributions, or using sham acquisition, financing or advisory arrangements to reduce French tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, statutory interest, surcharges generally ranging from 40% to 80%, and criminal tax-fraud penalties that may include imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with aggravated cases potentially reaching 7 years and EUR 3 million, subject to statutory aggravating conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and directors who personally participate in fraudulent conduct may face criminal prosecution, civil liability, tax recovery actions and professional disqualification. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be imposed by a court in appropriate criminal proceedings. Corporate limited liability does not protect intentional personal wrongdoing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold or remit cross-border withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties or other reportable French-source income to a non-resident without applying the correct withholding rate, relying on an invalid residence certificate, or failing to file Form 2777-SD.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the unpaid withholding tax from the French payer, late-payment interest, late filing and payment surcharges, potential gross-up liability, and increased penalties where the omission is deliberate or fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal liability where deliberate non-payment, gross negligence or fraudulent organization is established. A director may also face criminal exposure for falsification, concealment or participation in tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging unsupported management fees, royalties or interest, shifting SPAC sponsor profits offshore, providing guarantees without remuneration, or using non-arm's-length acquisition and financing terms.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary tax adjustment, denial of deductions, withholding tax exposure, interest, penalties, deemed-distribution treatment and possible documentation penalties. Inadequate transfer pricing documentation may permit a penalty generally equal to the greater of the statutory minimum and a percentage of the adjusted transactions or tax reassessment, subject to the applicable rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be pursued for intentional misrepresentation, abuse of corporate assets or fraudulent tax conduct. Mere failure to achieve a preferred transfer pricing outcome does not automatically create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and abuse of law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a French SARL with nominal directors, no genuine decision-making, no operational rationale, circular cash flows, conduit ownership, or artificial residence solely to access treaty or EU benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or directive relief, recharacterization of payments, corporate income tax reassessment, withholding tax, abuse-of-law surcharge potentially up to 80%, and invalidation of tax-neutral restructuring treatment where statutory conditions are not met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil claims, contribution actions in insolvency, management bans and criminal liability if they knowingly implement sham arrangements. The corporate veil is not automatically pierced merely because the company is thinly staffed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate asset misuse and unlawful profit extraction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using company funds for sponsor, director or shareholder expenses, paying fictitious advisory fees, making unlawful distributions, or extracting funds before legally distributable profits exist.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of misused assets, cancellation of unlawful distributions, tax reassessment, civil damages and, where applicable, criminal penalties for misuse of company assets or distribution of fictitious dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: SARL managers can be personally liable for management faults and unlawful distributions. Criminal sanctions may include imprisonment and fines under French company-law provisions, with additional bans on management. Travel bans are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting anonymous or unexplained investor funds, failing to identify beneficial owners, processing unusual SWIFT wires, misusing escrow accounts, ignoring sanctions indicators, or failing to report suspicious transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory enforcement, administrative fines, supervisory measures, freezing or blocking of funds, criminal money-laundering penalties and confiscation. Serious money laundering may carry imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 375,000, with aggravated cases carrying higher sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and compliance officers may face criminal liability for knowing participation, concealment or negligent failure where legally relevant. Courts may order asset confiscation, management bans and restrictions on movement in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making payments to sanctioned persons, jurisdictions or banks, acquiring restricted assets, or disguising the ultimate investor or beneficiary through nominee or layered entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Asset freezes, payment blocking, administrative and criminal fines, imprisonment, confiscation and regulatory restrictions under applicable French and EU sanctions legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and authorized signatories may be personally prosecuted where they authorized, facilitated or knowingly ignored a prohibited transaction. Corporate authorization does not eliminate personal criminal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misstating acquisition targets, fair values, liabilities, escrow balances, sponsor promote arrangements, contingent obligations or going-concern status in statutory accounts or investor documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restatement, tax reassessment, civil damages, regulatory sanctions and criminal penalties for false accounts or dissemination of misleading information. Consequences may include fines, imprisonment and director disqualification depending on the offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and directors approving knowingly false accounts may be personally liable to the company, creditors and investors and may face criminal prosecution. Directors' and officers' insurance cannot generally cover deliberate fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful distribution or failure to preserve capital
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing cash, sponsor promote or acquisition proceeds without approved accounts and distributable reserves, or continuing distributions while statutory net assets are below required thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of distributions, civil liability, corporate-law penalties and potential criminal liability for fictitious dividends or related misconduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: SARL managers may be jointly or personally liable for unlawful distributions and resulting creditor loss. Management bans and criminal sanctions may apply in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Destruction or withholding of tax and accounting records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to preserve invoices, bank statements, board minutes, investor records, transfer pricing files, beneficial-owner evidence and transaction documentation, or obstructing a tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment based on available information, rejection of deductions, adverse evidentiary presumptions, procedural penalties, obstruction penalties and increased tax surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for obstruction, document destruction or fraudulent concealment. Authorities may seek judicial measures and criminal sanctions where intentional obstruction is established.
